explanations.explanation: Right, friend. The writer opens with "if you accept my words…" (Proverbs 2:1). Accepting comes before anything else in this whole chain of IFs. You can't unpack a cookie box you never took off the porch.

Good thinking, but writing isn't in the verse. The text says "if you accept my words and hide my commandments within you" (Proverbs 2:1). The first step is taking the words in. I've seen plenty of recipes copied out neatly and never baked once, friend.

Daily recitation sounds nice, but that's not what the verse says. It says "if you accept my words and hide my commandments within you" (Proverbs 2:1). The words go inside, not just out loud. The first IF is about receiving them.

Close, friend, but the verse goes the other way. It says "if you truly call out to insight and lift your voice to understanding" (Proverbs 2:3). The son isn't sitting quietly. He's calling out and lifting his voice. Nobody finds treasure by whispering at the ground.

That's right. The verse says "if you truly call out to insight and lift your voice to understanding" (Proverbs 2:3). The son uses his voice. He calls out and lifts it. No waiting in silence here, friend.
Yes, friend. The writer says "if you seek it like silver and search it out like hidden treasure" (Proverbs 2:4). Silver and buried treasure are things people dig for. Nobody finds those by accident.

explanations.answer: Grain in a time of famine
explanations.explanation: That's a believable guess, but grain isn't in this verse. The writer says "if you seek it like silver and search it out like hidden treasure" (Proverbs 2:4). It's silver and hidden treasure. Both are things you dig for.

Water in the wilderness would make anybody search hard, but it's not what the verse says. It says "if you seek it like silver and search it out like hidden treasure" (Proverbs 2:4). The comparison is silver and hidden treasure.
Yes, friend. Verse 5 says "then you will discern the fear of the LORD and discover the knowledge of God." (Proverbs 2:5). All that searching ends in knowing God. That beats any treasure chest.

Honor sounds like a nice prize, but this verse doesn't mention it. It says "then you will discern the fear of the LORD and discover the knowledge of God." (Proverbs 2:5). The reward is the knowledge of God.
A seat among the elders isn't in this verse, friend. It says "then you will discern the fear of the LORD and discover the knowledge of God." (Proverbs 2:5). The prize is knowing God.

That's it, friend. "For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding." (Proverbs 2:6). The son does the searching, and the LORD does the giving. Wisdom is never something we cook up on our own.
A king isn't named anywhere in this verse. It says "For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding." (Proverbs 2:6). The giver is the LORD, friend.
No prophet shows up in this verse, friend. It says "For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding." (Proverbs 2:6). Wisdom comes from the LORD Himself.

True, friend. Verse 8 says He acts "to guard the paths of justice and protect the way of His saints." (Proverbs 2:8). The LORD guards justice and protects His saints. That's a good thing to have on your side.
Not quite, friend. Verse 8 says He acts "to guard the paths of justice and protect the way of His saints." (Proverbs 2:8). So the LORD does guard the paths of justice. It's true.

I get why you'd think so, friend, because knowledge can sound like homework. But the verse says "wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will delight your soul." (Proverbs 2:10). Delight is the opposite of a heavy load. So this one is false.

That's right. The verse says "wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will delight your soul." (Proverbs 2:10). Knowledge doesn't weigh the soul down. It delights it. That's the kind of weight I'd carry all day, friend.
Yes, friend. Verse 11 says "Discretion will watch over you, and understanding will guard you." (Proverbs 2:11). Those two stand watch over him. That's quite a security team.

Angels and chariots would make a dramatic entrance, but they're not in this verse. It says "Discretion will watch over you, and understanding will guard you." (Proverbs 2:11). The guards are discretion and understanding.

Friends are a blessing, but this verse doesn't name them as the guards. It says "Discretion will watch over you, and understanding will guard you." (Proverbs 2:11). Discretion and understanding do the guarding, friend.
True, friend. Verse 14 describes them as "those who enjoy doing evil and rejoice in the twistedness of evil." (Proverbs 2:14). They enjoy it and rejoice in it. I'd call that a sad kind of party.
Not quite, friend. Verse 14 says they are "those who enjoy doing evil and rejoice in the twistedness of evil." (Proverbs 2:14). So they do enjoy it, and the answer is true.
That's the word, friend. Verse 15 says "whose paths are crooked and whose ways are devious." (Proverbs 2:15). The paths they walk are crooked, and they're nothing like the straight paths they left.
Level sounds smooth and pleasant, but it's not the word here. Verse 15 says "whose paths are crooked and whose ways are devious." (Proverbs 2:15). Crooked is the word, friend.
Narrow is a good guess, but it's not in this verse. It says "whose paths are crooked and whose ways are devious." (Proverbs 2:15). These paths are crooked, friend.

Yes, friend. Verse 17 says she "abandons the partner of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God." (Proverbs 2:17). Both are things she leaves behind. This is a heavy part, and I think it's a sad picture.

explanations.answer: The way back to her city
explanations.explanation: Her city isn't mentioned here, friend. Verse 17 says she "abandons the partner of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God." (Proverbs 2:17). What she forgets is the covenant of her God.
Her father's name isn't in this verse, friend. It says she "abandons the partner of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God." (Proverbs 2:17). The covenant of her God is what she forgets.

I wish that were what it said, friend, but it's the other way. Verse 19 says "None who go to her return or negotiate the paths of life." (Proverbs 2:19). So the answer is false. It's a serious warning.

That's right, friend. Verse 19 says "None who go to her return or negotiate the paths of life." (Proverbs 2:19). Nobody who goes to her comes back to the paths of life. It's a heavy warning, and that's why wisdom guards the son from it.

Yes, friend. Verse 20 says "So you will follow in the ways of the good, and keep to the paths of the righteous." (Proverbs 2:20). Wisdom leads him to walk with good people. That's a crowd worth joining.
Strong is a fine word, but it's not the one here. Verse 20 says "So you will follow in the ways of the good, and keep to the paths of the righteous." (Proverbs 2:20). The word is good, friend.
Rich isn't the word here, friend. Verse 20 says "So you will follow in the ways of the good, and keep to the paths of the righteous." (Proverbs 2:20). It's the ways of the good.

explanations.answer: They inhabit the land and remain in it
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Verse 21 says "the upright will inhabit the land, and the blameless will remain in it." (Proverbs 2:21). They live there and they stay. Sounds like a home that sticks.

explanations.answer: They leave the land for a far country
explanations.explanation: Leaving is the opposite of what the verse says. It says "the upright will inhabit the land, and the blameless will remain in it." (Proverbs 2:21). The upright stay in the land, friend.

explanations.answer: They build cities across the land
explanations.explanation: Cities aren't mentioned in this verse. It says "the upright will inhabit the land, and the blameless will remain in it." (Proverbs 2:21). They inhabit it and remain in it, friend.

True, friend. Verse 22 says "but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the unfaithful will be uprooted." (Proverbs 2:22). The wicked are cut off and the unfaithful are uprooted. It's the sober ending to the two paths.
Not this time, friend. Verse 22 says "but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the unfaithful will be uprooted." (Proverbs 2:22). The wicked are cut off from the land, so it's true.
